beats: A CRA notice says you owe five thousand dollars. Before you pay, or panic, let's investigate.
Suspect one: a forgotten T5. Fifteen thousand dollars of interest you never reported. At about thirty-three percent, that's nearly the whole bill.
Suspect two: a payment that went to another year. Your CRA account shows where each payment landed.
Suspect three: instalments. Owe over three thousand dollars this year and in one of the last two? CRA expected payments during the year.
The twist: you have time. No legal collection for ninety days, and you can object at least that long. But interest compounds daily from April thirtieth.
Open the notice, read the explanation of changes, match every slip, then pay or object.
Next: the filing deadlines that cost you money. Follow so you don't miss it.
